CodeNomad is the command center that puts AI coding on steroids.

CodeNomad is the command center that puts AI coding on steroids.
CodeNomad 1.1.0 - Design, memory and event-driven Missions
Create images in a dedicated Design workspace, carry useful knowledge between conversations, and let Missions respond to schedules and repository activity. CodeNomad 1.1 also makes long conversations more responsive and keeps your workspace easier to recover across project tabs, browser reloads and mobile app switches.
Before upgrading
- OpenCode 2.3.0 is the minimum and recommended runtime. CodeNomad 1.1 refuses 2.2.x services. Updating CodeNomad does not update or restart OpenCode: review Settings > OpenCode, install or select a compatible executable, and explicitly restart the shared service when needed. That restart can interrupt other connected clients (#1491).
- The remotely updated 1.1 interface requires a CodeNomad 1.1.0+ server. Older servers retain their cached or bundled interface until the application/server is updated.
- Memory is off by default. Design requires the separately installed and enabled panel extension and suitable configured models. Requests prepared by the Design panel remain editable until you send them.
- Windows packages ship without production code signing. Windows may show an unknown-publisher warning.
Design and Images
- Use the Design agent and image skills from the Design panel, with an Images conversation for each project folder or worktree.
- Browse images, prepare follow-up requests, compare results and inspect image lineage where it can be verified. Local-file Markdown images render directly in the transcript (#1196, #1201, #1202, #1203, #1204, #1205).
Optional local agent memory
- Save useful facts, preferences and references in separate About you and Project scopes. Worktrees of the same repository share project memory.
- Review, edit and tidy entries in Settings, with a local change history. Disabling Memory keeps saved entries and removes its tool from the agent's catalogue; enabling or disabling it updates running sessions without restarting OpenCode. The entry list folds under Entries, with its New, Modified and Needs review badges shown on the summary (#1313, #1479, #1572).
Missions that run on schedules and events
- Combine schedules and events with or / if / else, time zones and fallback schedules. Armed native schedules can run with CodeNomad closed while OpenCode and the execution host remain available (#1259, #1291, #1350).
- Trigger work from new or merged pull/merge requests and new issues on GitHub, GitLab or Gitea, with optional author filters. GitHub.com also supports account notifications and Dependabot alerts. Checks use the execution host's forge access (#1461, #1466).
- Continue scheduled work in an Existing session, preserving its conversation, title and permissions, or start a fresh coordinator for each passage. Add and edit Followed conversations before the first launch, including for an immediate Mission (#1461, #1545).
- Follow tasks and results in a single tree, open the conversation needing your answer, and read summaries or detailed playbook instructions. Waiting, running, paused, interrupted and unconfirmed states have distinct labels and recovery actions (#1381, #1391, #1507, #1542, #1544).
- Agents can do everything the Missions editor and panel offer: prepare Missions with automatic start or schedules, control existing Missions and schedules, and use saved configurations and Missions settings from any conversation of the project (#1551).
- Creation, preference saves and interrupted schedule wakes recover through their original requests instead of creating replacement work. Human questions stay with the coordinator, and each scheduled passage retains its own journal and result (#1227, #1482, #1540, #1547).
Integrations managed from Plugins
- Manage native integrations from Status > Plugins. Each row shows the installed package version and a clickable application/document state: install or update the application part, attach to a compatible open document, or detach the displayed conversation. Native first-use attachment remains available (#1492, #1509).
- Add native plugin packages, control Global or Project activation where supported, and explicitly check for package updates. Git-installed packages show their version or a short commit identifier; details retain the full commit. Application installation and plugin removal require confirmation (#1232, #1239, #1556).
- Provider usage includes additional quota readers, OpenCode Console's reported counts and credit balance, and a labelled estimate for OpenCode Zen free usage. Explicit model choices survive a loading catalogue. An active /goal stays on one line above Tokens in Status (#1309, #1312, #1317, #1455, #1521).
Clearer, more responsive conversations
- Background subagent cards show intermediate and final reports and keep tracking the child until settlement. Watched child transcripts update while streaming (#1464, #1491, #1534).
- Long sessions open more smoothly through deferred highlighting and tool rendering. Scrolling and Latest keep following streamed replies, and an older repair read preserves text already received (#1486, #1500, #1520, #1538).
- Render Mermaid diagrams locally, switch between source and diagram, and preview .mmd files. Click project-file links in replies to open the file reader. Code Mode JSON is easier to read, and interrupted shell calls retain their output separately from the stop notice (#1469, #1485, #1491).
- Archive conversations without deleting their history, navigate between user messages, and delete long-context sessions more responsively (#1406, #1449, #1484).
A workspace that stays yours
- Open the same project or conversation in multiple tabs with independent views, scroll positions, panel choices and Mission readers. Keep chat in one tab and a file, web preview or report in another; duplicate tabs share one live web preview per conversation, and messages and execution remain shared (#1510, #1571).
- With Restore previous state enabled, a browser/PWA tab restores its projects, selected conversations, drafts and reading positions after a page reload or mobile page discard. A new tab or fully closed PWA starts on the home page (#1515).
- Closing a project tab keeps its unsent drafts and attachments available when you reopen that folder in the same window. These closed-project drafts are temporary, not part of startup restoration (#1522).
- Contrast works across palettes: Auto follows the system preference, On increases contrast and Off keeps normal rendering. It preserves your selected palette and editable colours (#1569, #1570).
Desktop, diagnostics and access
- Startup shows the actual backend state and offers OpenCode settings when recovery is needed. Setup separates the installed CLI from the running service, and logs and background-command output open in non-modal windows (#1467, #1528, #1531, #1560).
- Launch at startup can start OpenCode when you sign in; keeping the computer awake is a separate opt-in desktop setting. Windows Tauri displays a boot splash during delayed startup, and Linux Tauri supports pasted images/files and avoids menu-bar overlap (#1288, #1290, #1307, #1470, #1503).
- Remote HTTP windows support Mission creation and OAuth link copying. Administrators can disable Remote Control and lock the listening address. Trusted direct HTTPS access can opt in to SideCars; enable this only for users trusted to use those services (#1474, #1489, #1523, #1525).
- Desktop runtimes and security-sensitive dependencies have been updated. Process ownership, listener-origin checks and proxy destination validation are hardened, alongside Linux GLib and packaging fixes (#1457, #1458, #1459, #1473, #1543, #1552).
History, search, navigation, Images and technical cleanup support OpenCode's optional split assistant-part storage. Plugin readiness handles accumulated backend presence records, and assistant text stays searchable with the updated SQLite runtime (#1359, #1453, #1490).
Support CodeNomad
CodeNomad is free and open source, maintained full time by Pascal Andr├®. You can support its continued development through GitHub Sponsors or Ko-fi.
Full changelog: v1.0.1...v1.1.0

- feat(design): register the Design agent and skills at plugin load, driven by backend leases by @pascalandr in #1202
